title: HTTP Method Manipulation on change_password Endpoint
description: The /api/change_password.php endpoint accepts and processes all HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, HEAD) without proper method validation. The endpoint should only accept POST requests for changing a user's password, but instead accepts any HTTP method with HTTP 200 responses. The endpoint processes all methods identically, returning the same "User not authenticated" message regardless of which HTTP method is used.
impact: An attacker could use non-standard HTTP methods to bypass WAF rules or security filters designed to restrict certain methods. The use of GET method to change a password could enable CSRF attacks if a user clicks a malicious link, as GET requests are typically sent by browsers automatically. Additionally, PUT/DELETE/PATCH methods can be used to bypass method-based access controls. This violates REST API principles where GET should be idempotent (read-only operations only).
evidence:
POC execution confirmed the vulnerability. Testing the /api/change_password.php endpoint with various HTTP methods all return HTTP 200:
- GET /api/change_password.php → HTTP 200 (should be 405 Method Not Allowed)
- POST /api/change_password.php → HTTP 200 (acceptable)
- PUT /api/change_password.php → HTTP 200 (should be 405)
- DELETE /api/change_password.php → HTTP 200 (should be 405)
- PATCH /api/change_password.php → HTTP 200 (should be 405)
- HEAD /api/change_password.php → HTTP 200 (should be 405)

Response body is identical for all methods: {"success": false, "message": "User not authenticated."} indicating the endpoint processes all methods identically without validation.
references: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type, OWASP API Security - API5:2023 Broken Function Level Access Control, HTTP Method Manipulation attacks
toolCallDescription: Documenting HTTP method manipulation vulnerability on change_password endpoint with POC evidence
